# TildaZ v0.7.0

**GPU rendering on Linux, and a command menu in every window.**

v0.7.0 changes two things you notice immediately. Linux now draws through the
GPU instead of a software buffer, so scrolling and typing cost a fraction of
the CPU they used to and startup is roughly three times faster. And every
window — even with a single tab — carries a small `[+][×][…]` control strip
whose `…` opens a command menu listing the common actions and their shortcuts.
Inline tab renaming is gone, and the Windows zip has a new file layout. The
config schema is unchanged.

## GPU rendering on Linux

TildaZ on Linux now renders with OpenGL ES through `zwp_linux_dmabuf_v1`,
replacing the software `wl_shm` path that shipped in v0.5.0. It is the default
and was verified on AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA hardware.
([#277](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/277))

- **Less CPU.** Scrolling drops from 5.8% to 1.5% CPU and typing from 10.2% to
  2.6% on the reference machine.
- **Faster startup.** Cold start went from 201 ms to 66 ms, a 67% reduction,
  after fontconfig is initialized once per process and dialog fonts are built
  only when a dialog opens.
  ([#368](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/368))
- **Less memory bandwidth.** TildaZ negotiates compressed buffer formats when
  the driver offers them (AMD DCC, Intel CCS). Measured with DCC on AMD, GPU
  frame time drops 4.6× at 1600×900 and 13.3× at 4K compared with an
  uncompressed tiled buffer — the larger the display, the bigger the gain.
  ([#367](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/367),
  [#369](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/369))
- **Cheaper frames on large screens.** Building a frame at 4K is 51% faster
  when scrolling and 68% faster when typing, because blank trailing cells are
  skipped and glyph lookups are cached.
  ([#362](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/362))

Rendering falls back to software automatically when a compositor or driver
cannot provide the GPU path, and `TILDAZ_DISABLE_GPU=1` forces the old
`wl_shm` renderer. The startup log records which path was chosen
(`render_path=gpu-gl`, `gpu-dmabuf`, or `software-shm`).

## Command menu and single-tab controls

- A `[+][×][…]` control strip now sits in the top-right corner of every window.
  Previously the tab controls appeared only once a second tab existed. With one
  tab the strip overlays the corner without reserving a tab bar or moving the
  terminal grid. ([#329](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/329))
- `…` opens a command menu with Show / Hide TildaZ, New Tab, Close Active Tab,
  Copy Selection, Paste, Toggle Full Screen, Open Config, Keyboard Shortcuts,
  and About TildaZ. Each row shows its keyboard shortcut, and the first row
  shows the global hotkey this instance is actually configured with rather
  than assuming F1.
- The menu takes the keyboard while it is open: `Esc` closes,
  `Up` / `Down` / `Home` / `End` / `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` move, and
  `Enter` / `Space` runs the focused command. Clicking outside — including
  right-click — only closes the menu and does not paste. On a short window the
  menu trims whole rows and scrolls with the wheel, arrow keys, or a click on
  the chevron rows.
- At the 32-tab limit `+` now stays in place and turns gray instead of
  disappearing, so the controls no longer shift position.

## Tab bar and tab titles

- The tab bar is one continuous strip: every tab shares the bar's background
  and the active tab is marked by a TildaZ amber underline instead of a
  lighter background. Tab slots are separated by vertical dividers.
  ([#334](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/334))
- Tab bar and menu colors are now derived from your theme's background
  brightness, so light themes get a light chrome instead of the fixed dark
  gray. ([#335](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/335))
- A tab being dragged now floats above its neighbors with an opaque
  background, an intact underline, and its title on top.
  ([#343](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/343))
- Long tab titles are clipped at the tab boundary instead of the whole glyph
  disappearing when it would not fit.
- **Inline tab renaming was removed.**
  ([#341](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/341)) Tab titles follow the
  shell through OSC 0/2 window titles, which most shells and programs such as
  vim or ssh already set. To set one yourself, use your shell — for example
  `printf '\033]0;my title\007'`.
- A new tab is labeled `Tab N` the moment it opens, and the shell's first
  title appears without the extra delay v0.6.2 had.
  ([#364](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/364))

## Consistent rendering across platforms

- Transparent windows now composite identically on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
  The three platforms previously rounded alpha three different ways, so the
  same opacity produced slightly different colors.
  ([#353](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/353))
- The terminal grid no longer draws under the scrollbar, so the last column is
  fully visible and matches where clicks land.
  ([#350](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/350))
- The scrollbar thumb is visible on light themes — it now derives its color
  from the background instead of being a fixed 30% white — and its top and
  bottom margins are symmetric.
  ([#346](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/346),
  [#344](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/344))
- At fractional scale factors, one-point lines such as tab dividers and menu
  separators keep an even thickness instead of varying with their position.
  ([#357](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/357))
- Glyphs that overflow their cell are overlapped the same way everywhere; on
  Linux the right-hand side was being erased.
  ([#361](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/361))
- On Linux the window no longer overscans by one physical pixel at integer
  scale factors, which had cut off the last column of the scrollbar.
  ([#351](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/351))

## Windows

- The bundled ConPTY runtime (`conpty.dll` and `OpenConsole.exe`) moved into an
  `_internal\` folder, so the zip has exactly one executable at the top level
  and there is no longer any doubt about which file to run. TildaZ loads the
  runtime by absolute path, and refuses to start with a clear dialog if either
  file is missing rather than quietly degrading to the system console host.
  ([#339](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/339))
- If Direct3D 11 cannot create a hardware device, the renderer retries with
  WARP, Microsoft's built-in software rasterizer, instead of leaving an empty
  window. Only when both fail does TildaZ show an error and exit.
  ([#363](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/363))
- Official release builds now enable the SIMD VT parser. On the upstream
  `terminal-stream` benchmark, bulk output parses 13.0× faster for ASCII and
  1.7× faster for UTF-8; input dominated by OSC sequences is about 5% slower.
  ([#19](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/19))

## Linux desktop integration

- **KDE Plasma** hotkeys are registered directly with KGlobalAccel instead of
  going through the XDG Desktop Portal. This avoids the case where switching
  between KDE Plasma and another desktop in one session left the hotkey dead
  until the portal services or the machine restarted.
  ([#244](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/244))
- Changing a monitor's resolution now recomputes the drop-down's geometry
  instead of reusing the stale work area, and the GNOME and Cinnamon Shell
  extensions reposition the window to match.
  ([#356](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/356),
  [#373](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/373))
- A small `height_percent` window no longer closes before it is mapped on
  fractional-scale displays.
  ([#336](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/336))
- With the Cinnamon extension active, `hidden_start` is handled by the same
  owner as on GNOME. ([#327](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/327))
- On GNOME and Cinnamon, the first hotkey press hides a visible window even
  when another application currently has focus. The Shell extensions now
  decide by visibility, matching every other desktop.
- Right-click and command-menu paste go through the same input policy as the
  keyboard shortcut, so an in-progress IME composition is committed before the
  pasted text is inserted.
  ([#333](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/333),
  [#340](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/340))

## Upgrade notes

- **Windows: keep the `_internal` folder.** Unzip the release and keep
  `_internal\` next to `tildaz.exe`. Copying `tildaz.exe` out on its own no
  longer works — TildaZ shows a "Cannot Start" dialog and exits instead of
  falling back to the slower system console host.
- **Inline tab renaming is gone.** Titles set by double-clicking a tab in
  v0.6.2 and earlier cannot be set that way anymore. Use your shell's window
  title (OSC 0/2) instead.
- **Linux: unrecognized desktops need a manual binding.** The generic portal
  hotkey fallback was removed. KDE Plasma, GNOME, Cinnamon, COSMIC, Hyprland,
  and sway are unaffected — each already used its own native path. On a
  desktop TildaZ does not recognize, bind `tildaz --toggle N` yourself in that
  desktop's keyboard settings.
- **Linux: the GPU path is the default.** If a driver or compositor
  combination misbehaves, `TILDAZ_DISABLE_GPU=1` restores the v0.6.2 software
  renderer. Please report the case so it can be fixed rather than worked
  around.
- The macOS artifact keeps the stable self-signed TildaZ identity introduced
  in v0.6.2. It is still not Apple-notarized, so the documented first-launch
  Gatekeeper steps still apply.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Linux portable (glibc 2.28+) | `tildaz-v0.7.0-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}.tar.gz` | Extract and run `./install.sh`; no `sudo`. |
| Linux Debian / Ubuntu | `tildaz_0.7.0-1_{amd64,arm64}.deb` | Install with `dpkg` or a graphical software installer. |
| Linux Fedora / RHEL / openSUSE | `tildaz-0.7.0-1.{x86_64,aarch64}.rpm` | Install with `dnf` or the distro package tool. |
| Linux distro-independent | `TildaZ-0.7.0-{x86_64,aarch64}.AppImage` | Make executable and run; FUSE is optional. |
| Arch / Manjaro / EndeavourOS | `tildaz-0.7.0-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst` | x86_64 package. |
| macOS 14+ universal | `tildaz-v0.7.0-macos.dmg` | Apple Silicon and Intel; stable self-signed identity, not notarized. |
| Windows 10/11 x64 | `tildaz-v0.7.0-win-x64.zip` | Unzip and keep `_internal\` next to `tildaz.exe`. |
| Windows 11 ARM64 | `tildaz-v0.7.0-win-arm64.zip` | ARM64-native binary; same layout as the x64 zip. |

## Known limitations

- Text attributes beyond bold and reverse are not applied yet: underline
  styles ([#365](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/365),
  [#374](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/374)), italic and bold font
  faces ([#375](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/375)), and blink
  ([#376](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/376)).
- [#366](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/366): a new tab starts in the
  shell's default directory, not the active tab's current directory.
- [#266](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/266): TildaZ does not answer
  terminal queries such as DA1, DSR, or OSC color requests, which can delay
  fish shell startup by about ten seconds on Linux and macOS.
- [#347](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/347): on Cinnamon, a session
  that reports no keyboard or pointer capability at login can leave input dead
  with no retry path.
- [#194](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/194): on Linux, Korean IME
  input can stop working after focusing an X11 Electron window such as VSCode
  (fcitx5 frontend separation).
- On Linux, yielding z-order on focus loss is not implemented —
  `zwlr_layer_shell_v1` layers have no normal-window slot.
